title: SE Enablement - Messaging & Demo Practice
summary: Internal SE enablement session to align AE/SE on messaging, rehearse demo flow for upcoming customer POC, and refine answers to common competitive and security questions. Practiced dedicated vs hosted positioning and objections around latency/cost and VPC/on-prem requirements.
transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-10 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim, Priya Rao, Omar Vazquez (Redwood) -- Lena Ortiz, Markus Eriksson, Sam Patel, Aisha Khan (Nimbus)
Recording: (internal link)

--- Auto Summary (brief) ---
- Goal: tighten messaging and demo flow for Nimbus POC.
- Focus: highlight Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private differences, fallback policies, cost/levers (batching, quant profiles), and SOC2/SAML talking points.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jared: okay thanks everyone for joining, uh kicking off the enablement. we got about 60 minutes, the plan is quick messaging sync, then demo practice, then Q&A. Priya you good?
[00:18] Priya: yep, all set. i'll lead the demo and Omar will jump in on any product nuance.
[00:28] Markus: sounds good. quick note, we're here to help your decks be crisp for our upcoming run with nimbus but also to make sure security lines up. aisha's on for that.
[00:40] Aisha: thanks, i'll flag anything that could be sticky from audit or data residency angles.
[00:48] Jared: great. starting with core message - 30 second elevator: "Redwood is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM inference predictable across hosted, dedicated and private deployments". priya, want to run the 30s?
[01:03] Priya: sure. "Redwood provides a unified runtime for high-performance inference - low latency, predictable costs, and consistent tooling across hosted API, Reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. We focus on operational controls like routing, KV cache, batching, and rollout tools so teams don't have to build that infra themselves."
[01:28] Jared: yeah that hits most points. maybe add a short line on our cost levers - batching, prefix caching, quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
[01:39] Priya: "and we surface quantization and batching recommendations through Redwood Optimize to cut unit cost without major quality regressions".
[01:48] Lena: that's solid. i just want guardrails for our reps - like what do we say when customers push on, you know, 'why not OpenAI or Anthropic?'.
[01:59] Omar: good question. competitive framing - two angles: model access & control, and operational economics. OpenAI/Anthropic give great models and simple hosted apis, but Redwood differentiates on predictable throughput (Dedicated) and private deployments for compliance. For teams wanting fine-grained routing, fallbacks and cost controls, Redwood is stronger.
[02:21] Priya: also call out latency SLOs on Dedicated and that we have automated fallback policies so apps remain online if capacity is low.
[02:32] Markus: and what about self-hosting on raw infra? customers occasionally say 'we'll just run it ourselves on SageMaker or raw k8s'.
[02:42] Jared: reply: you can, but we surface a lot of ops you won't get for free - continuous batching, optimized kernels, caching semantics, and the model catalog with validated performance. plus the engineering cost to keep that reliable often outweighs reserved capacity.
[02:58] Sam: can you quantify that? rough numbers or TCO?
[03:04] Omar: we usually avoid hard blanket numbers, but we show unit-token cost curves and a case study where dedicated reduced per-token cost by 30% vs ad-hoc self-hosting once ops and reliability overhead are included. we can hand them a benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:20] Jared: this is a good time to practice the demo. Priya, start the flow as if nimbus is in the call and ask clarifying q's.
[03:28] Priya: ok demo start: "we'll show a hosted flow first, then flip to Dedicated and Private deployment differences, and finish with the Redwood Console observability and Optimize suggestions."
[03:39] [Demo walkthrough - screen share simulated in transcript]
[03:45] Priya: (narrating) here's the Redwood API quickstart, the SDK call looks like fetch redwood.generate({...}) - we call out streaming responses and function-style outputs. sometimes i say 'fetch' and folks think i'm literally using browser fetch, so note that in messaging.
[04:10] Lena: small nit: make sure to call out that streaming means tokens appear progressively and we can hook tracing for latency analysis. Aisha, that's relevant for audit.
[04:22] Aisha: yes please call that out. also clarify data at rest encryption and KMS/HSM integration when you mention Private.
[04:33] Priya: good point. i'll add 'data at rest encrypted with KMS, optional HSM for keys' when i demo Private.
[04:40] Priya: switching to Dedicated - here's the capacity pool dashboard, you can reserve X gpus, set autoscale and burst policies. show latency graphs... note sometimes our telemetry label is 'Rwood' or transcriber says 'Red wood' - minor but don't worry.
[04:58] Jared: ha, transcriber issue. continue.
[05:02] Priya: when we show KV cache we call it "KV cache (prefix caching)" - avoid saying 'k-v cash' in slides.
[05:12] Markus: good. how do we present rollback/rollout?
[05:17] Omar: rollout demo - canary deploy, compare outputs via evals; auto-fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes. emphasize that these are config knobs in the Console.
[05:30] Priya: demo script line: "we can set a canary at 10% traffic, run evaluation prompts, and if quality regresses or latency exceeds threshold, policy can roll back automatically."
[05:44] Sam: will that autoscaling and fallback add cost unpredictability?
[05:49] Jared: yes that's a common objection. answer: you can pin capacity for predictable billing under Dedicated; autoscale/burst are optional and you can set hard caps. plus Redwood Optimize provides cost impact estimates when you change batching or quantization.
[06:07] Lena: ok, let's roleplay typical customer objections. Priya, you're AE. i'll be CTO.
[06:14] Priya: (AE) "we're concerned about latency - can Redwood meet sub-100ms for our 512-token workloads?"
[06:22] Lena (CTO): "we'd need to see numbers and worst-case p95."
[06:26] Priya: "We have verified performance profiles in the model catalog with p50/p95 numbers for different seq lengths; for 512 tokens we recommend Dedicated with optimized kernels and quant profiles. we'll run a short benchmark during POC to validate your exact p95."
[06:40] Lena: that was ok. but remember to mention sequence-length distribution matters.
[06:44] Priya: good catch.
[06:46] [Timestamp jump - mid-demo practice]
[20:05] Priya: switching to security slide: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 in progress, SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC in Console, audit logs. aisha anything to add?
[20:18] Aisha: mention encryption in transit and at rest, customer-managed keys for Private, and VPC peering details for on-prem. also retention controls and the ability to disable logs for sensitive flows.
[20:33] Priya: perfect. also call out compliance pack link (we'll send).
[20:38] Jared: on contracts: for Dedicated we usually do monthly or annual reserved capacity with SLA tiers. bring up that pricing is usage + reserved capacity; we'll send a pricing sheet.
[20:51] Markus: tight. in the POC we will need a security questionnaire answered and for legal to see DPA. who owns that?
[20:58] Jared: i'll own the DPA and security pack; Omar will help with the technical answers. action item noted.
[21:08] Sam: demo question - when you say 'model catalog' do you host open models or do you integrate third-party endpoints?
[21:15] Omar: we host curated open models with performance profiles and occasionally surface cloud-hosted variants; we also support routing to third-party endpoints when customers need it. mention this carefully - don't imply we host closed-source vendor models.
[21:30] Priya: practice line: "we maintain a model catalog of vetted open models and maintain performance profiles so customers can pick the right tradeoff for cost vs quality."
[21:40] [Interruption, some crosstalk]
[21:52] Guest - Intern: sorry quick question - what's KV cache again?
[21:56] Priya: it's a token-level cache for recent prefixes, reduces recomputation; good for chat apps.
[22:05] [Midpoint recap]
[30:00] Jared: recap - messaging tightened, demo flow practiced, security answers noted. let's roleplay one more hard objection: "we already have a cloud contract, why pay you?'"
[30:12] Priya: "If you're already cloud-first, Redwood still reduces dev time and increases reliability - we have batching, kernel selection and cache semantics out of box, plus a console for observability you can ship quickly. Also, Dedicated offset hardware ops and Optimize can reduce per-token costs over time."
[30:35] Lena: ok good. can Priya be more specific: i want a canned line about 'time to value' - like 'ship in weeks vs months'.
[30:44] Priya: "Redwood gets you from prototype to production in weeks because we provide the serving runtime, orchestration, and console, versus months to build equivalent infra."
[30:56] [Demo closing practice]
[40:10] Priya: final demo slide: POC checklist - scope, success criteria, security docs, benchmark plan, timeline, contacts.
[40:20] Jared: let's walk through Nimbus POC specifics: success criteria?
[40:26] Lena: 1) p95 latency under 200ms for 256-token median workloads; 2) no PII leakage in 500 sample prompts; 3) cost per inference under $0.02/token equivalent (ballpark).
[40:40] Sam: we also need per-route RBAC and audit logs retained for 90 days.
[40:47] Aisha: plus data residency in eu-west for a subset of workloads.
[40:52] Omar: noted; good that you spelled those out - we'll align on a POC plan.
[41:00] [Wrap-up, next steps and action items called out live]
[50:05] Jared: ok next steps: we'll send the security pack and pricing, schedule an engineering benchmark call, and record a demo video for Nimbus.
[50:20] Priya: i'll update the demo script to include the SOC2 and KMS bullet on the Private slide.
[50:26] Lena: please also include the benchmark spreadsheet and a short one-pager on Dedicated vs Private decision tree.
[50:34] Jared: will do. any final quick Qs?
[50:40] Markus: none from me. thanks this was helpful.
[50:44] Jared: thanks everyone. end of session.

--- Action Items (as read aloud) ---
- Jared: send DPA and security pack + compliance links during EOD 3/12.
- Omar: prepare benchmark spreadsheet and p95 reference cases by 3/15.
- Priya: update demo script and record short demo video by 3/17.
- Lena: share POC success criteria doc with Jared by 3/12.

--- End of Transcript ---
